text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
- The Swiss parliament elected Justice Minister Arnold Koller president. Foreign minister Flavio Cotti was named Vice-President. Koller's reign will last for one year.
- Union Bank of Switzerland forecasts the Swiss economy will register zero growth in the first half of 1997, but there is growth potential for the stock exchange.

- Many representatives of major political parties said yesterday bilateral negotiations between Switzerland and Europe could be jeopardised because Peter Bodenmann, president of the Social Democratic party in Switzerland, went to Austria to discuss Switzerland's transport policy with leading Austrian polticians. Transport Minister Moritz Leuenberger, who is also member of the Social Democratic party, citicized Bodenmann. - Bankrupt financier Werner Ray will remain imprisioned on the Bahamas. His fifth request for freedom has been turned down by a Bahama court.
- Swiss construction company Neidhard will shut down and some 140 employees will be laid off.
- Swiss authorities rejected some 30,000 refugees at the Swiss border during World War II, a study by the Federal Archive said.
Earlier reports had talked of 10,000 people. Switzerland accomodated some 230,000 refugees during the war.
